organism.overview: Ricinus communis is a poisonous plant whose seeds can contain ricin. Toxicity is associated with ingestion or other exposure to plant material, not with venom delivery.
naturalHistory: It is a fast-growing plant cultivated and naturalized in warm regions.
Seeds are enclosed in distinctive spiny fruits.
Seed toxicity can vary with processing and exposure context.

deliveryMechanism.summary: Exposure can follow ingestion of seeds or other plant material containing toxic proteins.
sequence: Seeds or plant material are handled or consumed.
Toxic material reaches the gastrointestinal tract.
Absorbed toxin can disrupt cellular protein synthesis.

habitats.name: Warm disturbed habitats and cultivation
habitats.summary: Grows in warm climates and is cultivated in some regions.

ecologicalRoles.summary: Spiny fruits protect developing seeds and contribute to plant reproduction.

externalProfile.sourceLabel: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
summaryPoints: Ricin is a toxic protein associated with castor beans and requires exposure-specific evidence.
